description:
Olaf and Ollie are two adorable little astronauts who share a big love for space and adventure. Olaf, the curious and playful boy astronaut, dreams of exploring distant planets and discovering the mysteries of the universe. Olie, the sweet and imaginative girl astronaut, loves gazing at the stars and dreaming about galaxies far away.

Together, they sit side by side on the moon,  great adventure begins with a dream — and the best journeys are even more special when shared with someone you love.
summary: Curious Cosmo: Chasing the Light Horizon is an interactive, browser-based astronaut survival simulator and mission trainer that guides aspiring flight directors from the Lunar South Pole to Mars and out to Voyager 1's 1 Light-Day milestone. Powered by live NASA Open APIs and real aerospace physics models, players manage life-support trade-offs, complete hands-on engineering tasks, customize their spacesuit with earned NASA mission patches, and transmit a visual-audio Morse code beacon across interstellar space.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Curious Cosmo: Chasing the Light Horizon is an interactive, browser-based astronaut survival simulator and mission trainer built for aspiring flight directors. Guided by Cadet Sunny and Hoot the Space Owl, players progress through a 3-chapter deep-space journey—from the Lunar South Pole to Mars and out to Voyager 1's 1 Light-Day milestone—solving real aerospace life-support trade-offs and hands-on engineering mini-games:

- Chapter 1 (Lunar Base at Shackleton Crater): Syncs live solar flare alerts from NASA's DONKI API. Players balance oxygen reserves against radiation shielding and pump water-ice walls to watch live dosimeter readings drop in real time via the exponential radiation attenuation formula (D = D0 * e^(-μx)).

- Chapter 2 (Mars Outpost at Jezero Crater): Simulates a 14-minute one-way communication delay and connects daily resistive exercise (modeled on NASA OSDR microgravity research) to astronaut EVA stamina during a Martian dust-storm solar array cleanup.

- Chapter 3 (Interstellar Relay at Voyager 1): Tracks Voyager 1's real-time approach toward its historic 1 Light-Day (24-hour signal delay / 16.09 billion miles) milestone. Players calculate Plutonium-238 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG) decay (P(t) = P0 * e^(-λt)) and shed non-essential instrument loads to keep the Golden Record transmitter online.

- Spacesuit Locker, V-G-R Beacon & Certificate Export: Players unlock official-style mission patches (NASA Artemis, Mars Perseverance, and Voyager Golden Record), customize Sunny's suit colorway, transmit "V - G - R" in synthesized audio-visual Morse code across one light-day, and download a dynamically generated PDF Mission Certificate.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Deep-space exploration involves complex physics and physiological challenges that can feel abstract in textbooks. By turning real NASA open data and aerospace engineering equations into interactive cause-and-effect gameplay, Curious Cosmo makes space science accessible, memorable, and engaging for young learners and space enthusiasts—inspiring the next generation of mission planners and flight directors.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Languages & Core Web Standards: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) for lightweight, zero-install browser performance.

- Graphics & Audio APIs: HTML5 Canvas API (for dynamic spacesuit and circular mission patch compositing) and Web Audio API (for real-time Morse code synthesis and interactive sound effects).

- Libraries & Deployment: jsPDF for automated client-side PDF certificate generation, hosted statically via GitHub Pages.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

- Resilient Live-Data Architecture: Fetches live NASA DONKI solar flare classifications and NASA OSDR (Study OSD-48) metadata on launch while seamlessly falling back to curated NASA telemetry if offline or rate-limited, ensuring uninterrupted gameplay anywhere.

- Accessible Physics Visualization: Translates exponential radiation shielding and RTG half-life decay into intuitive interactive sliders, pumps, and live telemetry readouts rather than static equations.

- Zero-Barrier Access: Designed as a pure client-side web application so students, educators, and judges can launch and play immediately on any device without installations or logins.
dataRefs: NASA OSDR (Study OSD-48: Spaceflight Musculoskeletal Adaptation)
